lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1  Essential Business Writing Skills – Checklist  Introduction ü Communication is a critical skill in business ü The ability to clearly relay a message through writing is often overlooked ü Videos, podcasts, and images get a large portion of marketing press ü But business writing skills are crucial to success ü Most people first experience your business through your written content ü Poor writing makes a bad first impression and damages credibility ü People will perceive you as unprofessional and untrustworthy ü If written effectively however, your content will draw in potential customers  ü You generate more leads and convert more sales ü You must come across as knowledgeable, reliable, and professional  Learning Objectives:  ü Prepare appropriately before you write  ü Use the tone of voice that suits your audience ü Organize your thoughts into a logical flow ü Structure your writing for maximum clarity ü Identify and eliminate unnecessary words and phrases ü Ensure your writing is accurate and grammatically correct

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2  ü Grab and keep your readers' attention  ü Write persuasively to encourage action  ü Write enticing sales copy that converts ü Resolve sensitive situations in a polite and professional way  ü Write compelling content for common business writing formats ü Explain clearly to readers how to complete a process or task ü Consolidate and implement your learning and plan future action steps      Prerequisites Make sure that you have examples on hand of current writing you've done for different situations (blog posts, emails, sales copy, reports, etc.). Identify situations coming up or current where you need to write something for your business.    Expectations Before we start the course, take a minute to think about what you want to get out of it. In the Action Guide, write down three skills you expect to gain.

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  Module 1 - Before You Write a Word Lesson 1: What You Need to Know  Key Takeaway: Ø Preparation is key before you start writing. You need to know why and to whom you’re writing to ensure clear communication.  Learning Objective: ü Prepare appropriately before you write, so that you can ensure your writing resonates with your audience and achieves your goal  Choose the Right Medium for Your Purpose ü Effective communicators are always aware of two key elements: 1. Their context, which includes their audience 2. The purpose of their communication ü These elements dictate the means of communication, e.g. email, letter, phone, etc.  Understand Your Audience ü Tailor the content and the mode of communication to suit your audience ü Discover the words and phrases your audience uses ü Use their language in your writing, so they feel you and your message is relevant to them

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4  Think Globally ü Globalization has brought people from different cultural backgrounds much closer together  ü Your writing needs to be globally inclusive ü Avoid using any professional jargon or colloquialisms that wouldn’t resonate with someone on the other side of the globe ü Make a decision on the spelling and grammar standard you’ll use, e.g. US or UK ü Avoid technical terminology and acronyms  Prepare Your Communication for Your Audience ü Know what you want to say ü Know where you want to say it    ü Know what you want your readers to feel ü Know what you want your readers to do   Action Steps: 1. Briefly describe your ideal target audience. Write down what forms of communication you currently use and the style and type of language of the content. 2. Pick a piece of written content to create from start-to-finish by the end of the course. Get started in this lesson. Describe your audience for this piece, what you want to say (high level), your communication format, what you want readers to feel, and what they should do.

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5  Lesson 2: Pick the Appropriate Tone  Key Takeaway: Ø Be prepared to vary your tone to suit your audience and the content of your message so it’s appropriate to the readers and the circumstances.    Learning Objective: ü Achieve a professional tone of voice in your writing to suit your audience   Consider Your Grammar ü First, second, and third person point of view ü This is the perspective you use to address your reader, reflected by your pronouns. o 1st person uses Me, my, I, mine, myself, we, us, ours, ourselves o 2nd person uses You, yours, yourself, yourselves o 3rd person uses He, she, it, him, her, his, hers, himself, herself, itself, they, them ü Decide the purpose of your writing and choose the point of view that’s most appropriate ü Don’t mix points of view within a sentence  ü Your focus is on the reader, so first person and second person will have more impact.

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6  Active voice vs. passive voice ü Active voice: the subject of the sentence performs the action  ü Passive voice: the subject receives the action ü The active voice makes your writing lively, interesting, and dynamic ü Use the active voice as much as possible  ü The passive voice is dry and unengaging ü Passive is more appropriate for scientific and academic writing  Choose the Right Style ü Choose the style that’s appropriate to your audience and appropriate for your message ü Two main styles: formal and informal ü Informal: For when you know your audience well o Contractions- ‘don’t’ rather than ‘do not’, ‘can’t’ rather than ‘cannot’ o First (I, we, us, our) or second person (you, your) point of view o Short sentences o Conversational style o Direct  ü Formal: For complex documents, e.g. reports and proposals   o More complex content o Longer sentences o Objective and thorough

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7  o No contractions o Third person voice (her, his, their) o Active voice unless you’re writing a scientific or academic report o Summary of main points ü Each style has its own merits and usage depends on the tone you want to set  Suit Your Style to Your Audience ü You’ll be writing for different audiences: o Customers o Prospects o Suppliers o Professional colleagues ü The style you use to address each group will be different  ü Always  think: o Who’s my target audience? o What’s the best way to communicate my message? o Which delivery style does my topic need?  Develop Style Guidelines ü Write down your decisions in a guidelines document ü This will standardize your written content

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  Action Steps: 1. Complete the Formal and Informal Language Exercise in your Action Guide. 2. Look at the piece of writing you’ve chosen to work through in the course. Write a brief style guideline for this piece.

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9  Lesson 3: Organize Your Thoughts  Key Takeaway: Ø Creating an outline helps establish the structure and flow of your writing.  Learning Objective: ü Organize your thoughts into a logical flow   Start With an Outline ü Before you dive into writing any piece of content, start with an outline ü Organize your thoughts to get clear about what you want to say ü Brainstorm all the points you want to make  ü Outline them in a logical sequence so one thought flows into another   ü Especially important for longer pieces of writing like sales pages, reports, etc.  Use Your Outline ü Don’t create an outline and then ignore it ü Use it to guide you through your writing and to stay on topic  Use Transition Words ü Transition words are useful for improving the flow of your writing

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10  ü Use them within a sentence, to link sentences, and to connect paragraphs ü Examples:  o Additionally o However o As I mentioned earlier o To illustrate that point o To summarize    Action Steps: 1. Complete the Logical Flow Exercise in your Action Guide. 2. Create an outline for your ongoing piece of writing

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11  Module 2 – Write Like a Professional   Lesson 1: Structure  Key Takeaway: Ø A clear structure will keep your writing on track and lead your readers through the piece to its logical conclusion.   Learning Objective: ü Structure your writing for maximum clarity  Define a Clear Structure ü Whatever you’re writing, you need a basic structure  ü Divide your writing into paragraphs with one idea per paragraph ü State the purpose of your writing in the opening paragraph ü Vary the length of your sentences  ü Use your transitions    Layout Tips ü Write an attention-grabbing headline, e.g. o “How To …” o 7 Ways To …”

PAGE_12:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 12  o “5 Things You Didn’t Know About …” ü Use a headline generator for ideas ü Use subheadings  ü Use bullets  ü Use numbering  ü Follow the structure and layout of a formal document     Action Steps: 1. Choose an existing piece of your own writing, e.g. a blog post that gets a lot of viewers and readers. Critique your own structure and layout and make any necessary changes to improve it.   2. Write a dynamic headline and subheadings for your ongoing piece of writing and note where you’ll use bullet points or numbering to make it easy to understand at a glance.

PAGE_13:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 13  Lesson 2: Word Use  Key Takeaway: Ø Avoid redundant words and repetition, which can make your writing confusing and boring.
